poster_title: Rethinking Progression of Memory State in Robotic Manipulation: An Object-Centric Perspective
authors: Nhat Chung, Taisei Hanyu, Toan Nguyen, Huy Le, Frederick Bumgarner, Duy Minh Ho Nguyen, Khoa Vo, Kashu Yamazaki, Chase Rainwater, Tung Kieu, Anh Nguyen, Ngan Le

content: Current policies rely on recent sensory inputs, lacking long-term memory.
Short-horizon tasks dominate benchmarks, neglecting long-term dependencies.
Need for object-centric memory to handle repetitive steps and visually similar items.
Vision-language-action (VLA) models face scalability issues in non-Markovian settings.
Proposed work aims to evaluate and improve memory-augmented models.
panels.headline: Addressing the limitations of current visuomotor policies in non-Markovian environments

content: Current policies struggle with extended temporal dependencies.
Vision-language-action (VLA) models are intractable for tasks spanning hundreds of frames.
Repetitive steps and visually similar items pose significant challenges.
Need for a benchmark to evaluate memory-augmented models.
Token scaling issues in VLA models.

panels.headline: Challenges in non-Markovian robotic manipulation tasks

content: Introduction of LIBERO-Mem benchmark for non-Markovian tasks.
Proposal of Embodied-SlotSSM framework for object-centric memory.
Maintains spatio-temporally consistent slot identities.
Uses slot-state-space modeling and relational encoder.
Combines Slot Attention, Slot Fusion, and LLM Action Decoder.

content: Conducted in both Markovian and non-Markovian settings.
Assessed long-term dependencies and action prediction.
Compared with state-of-the-art VLA models.
Used LIBERO-Goal and LIBERO-Mem benchmarks.
Demonstrated practicality and scalability.

content: Embodied-SlotSSM shows improved performance on manipulation tasks.
Practical and scalable slot-based memory representations.

panels.headline: Enhanced stateful reasoning and long-horizon action prediction

content: Provides insights into non-Markovian reasoning in robotic manipulation.
LIBERO-Mem and Embodied-SlotSSM enhance stateful reasoning and efficiency.
Future work includes real-world validation.
Contributes to the development of memory-augmented models.
Highlights the importance of object-centric memory.
